meal.title: Variables as containers in C
meal.objective: Declare, assign, and reuse variables of basic types

voice.script: You have three pieces of data: a whole number, a decimal number, and a single letter. What if you could store a score, a temperature, and a letter, all in one program? How do you keep different kinds of data in a C program? A variable is just a container that holds a piece of data. The word int declares a container for whole numbers. The word double declares a container for numbers with fractions. The word char declares a container for a single character. A char array, written as char name[10], creates a container that can hold a sequence of characters, like a short word. Now see the code on screen: The program creates an int called score, sets it to 95, a double called temp set to 98.6, and a char called grade set to A. It also creates a char array called name and stores the word Alice. Finally it prints each container's contents. Running this prints the values we stored. Remember: a variable is a named container that holds a value of a specific type.
